hero.tagline: Canada's Biggest City, The World Cup's Biggest Party
hero.description: Toronto is Canada's cultural capital and one of the most ethnically diverse cities on Earth. BMO Field brings the 2026 tournament to a city where practically every competing nation has a passionate fan base living here. Expect the most multilingual crowd of any venue.

stadium.name: BMO Field
stadium.transport: Take the 509 or 511 streetcar from Union Station directly to Exhibition Place — about 15 minutes. GO Transit runs game-day service from the 905 suburbs. The stadium is a 10-minute walk from the Exhibition Place streetcar loop.

quick_facts.fan_hub_status: Major fan hub expected at Nathan Phillips Square; confirm local schedules

weather.june: Warm with highs in the mid-20s Celsius (high 70s Fahrenheit). Pleasant evenings, occasional rain.
weather.july: Hot and sometimes humid, highs around 27–29°C (80–84°F). Thunderstorms possible, especially in the afternoon.
packing_tips: Pack a light waterproof jacket — Toronto thunderstorms are fast and heavy
Sunscreen for afternoon fan zone events
Comfortable walking shoes — Downtown to Exhibition Place involves pavement
Layers for evening matches, which cool down quickly near the lake

airports.name: Toronto Pearson International Airport
transfer_options: UP Express train: Pearson to Union Station in 25 minutes, then streetcar to BMO Field
Rideshare from Pearson to Downtown takes 30–50 minutes depending on traffic
Taxis available at the terminal — roughly $60–70 to Downtown
airports.notes: Main international airport. UP Express is the fastest, most reliable option to the city. Buy your Presto card at the airport for seamless transit.

airports.name: Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport
transfer_options: Ferry to the mainland takes 2 minutes, then walk or short cab to BMO Field
Walking from the ferry terminal to BMO is about 20–25 minutes along the waterfront
Taxi or rideshare from the ferry is under 10 minutes
airports.notes: Island airport, mostly domestic routes. Extremely close to BMO Field and Harbourfront. Porter Airlines hub — excellent for fans flying from Montreal, Ottawa, or Halifax.

match_schedule.round: Group stage and possible advanced rounds
match_schedule.teams_or_placeholder: BMO Field hosts multiple matches. Official schedule released after group draw.

public_transit: 509 Harbourfront or 511 Bathurst streetcar from Union Station to Exhibition Place — most direct option
UP Express from Pearson to Union Station connects airport travellers in 25 minutes
GO Train extended match-day service from Mississauga, Hamilton, and Oshawa
rideshare: Rideshare pickup is on the east side of Exhibition Place — not directly at BMO Field
Surge pricing post-match is common — walk toward Dufferin St for quicker pickup
Lake Shore Blvd backs up after major matches — account for an extra 20–30 minutes
driving_parking: Exhibition Place has large parking lots — pre-book online
Traffic on the Gardiner Expressway and Lake Shore Blvd is severe after sold-out matches
Parking around Liberty Village fills quickly — arrive 90 minutes early if driving
walking_biking: Harbourfront path from Union Station to BMO Field takes about 25 minutes on foot
Bike Share Toronto (Bike Share) docks near the stadium and along the waterfront trail
The Martin Goodman Trail runs directly along the waterfront to Exhibition Place
match_day_tips: Arrive 90 minutes before kickoff — TTC streetcars are capacity-limited
Pre-pay for parking online to avoid the lineup on match day
Cell signal is strained inside BMO Field — download mobile tickets in advance

fan_hubs.name: Nathan Phillips Square Fan Festival
fan_hubs.location: 100 Queen St W, Toronto City Hall
fan_hubs.description: Toronto's iconic civic square — home to New Year's celebrations and major city events — is expected to host a major tournament fan hub with giant screens, live performances, and food representing every competing nation. The diverse crowd here will rival any venue atmosphere.
transport_tips: TTC Line 1 to Queen or Osgoode station — right at the square
Walking distance from most Downtown hotels
Large outdoor plaza — arrive early for best viewing position

fan_hubs.name: Harbourfront Fan Zone
fan_hubs.description: The Toronto Harbourfront area has outdoor screens, lakeside restaurants, and bars that will become organic fan hubs throughout the tournament. A pleasant spot for afternoon matches with lake views.
transport_tips: 10-minute walk from BMO Field after matches

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Core / Financial District
neighborhoods.best_for: Union Station access, major hotel brands, corporate rates
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe, busy, and well-lit 24/7. Major pedestrian corridors.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 509 or 511 streetcar from Union Station to BMO Field — 15 min
neighborhoods.description: Best access to both BMO Field (via streetcar) and Nathan Phillips Square (walking). Union Station connects to GO Train, UP Express, and TTC subway. Top choice for convenience.

neighborhoods.name: King West / Entertainment District
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe and very lively. Heavy pedestrian and bar traffic on match nights.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 511 Bathurst streetcar or 15-minute walk to BMO Field
neighborhoods.description: Toronto's most vibrant nightlife strip. King West and the Entertainment District have a dense concentration of sports bars and restaurants. Very walkable to BMO Field.

neighborhoods.name: Distillery District / St. Lawrence
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe neighbourhood with good transit. Cobblestone streets are charming but uneven.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Streetcar to Union, then 509 to BMO — about 30 min total
neighborhoods.description: A charming historic area east of Downtown with Victorian industrial architecture. Great for post-match dinners and the St. Lawrence Market. A bit farther from BMO but worth it for the experience.

neighborhoods.name: Kensington Market / College Street
neighborhoods.best_for: Budget travelers, eclectic atmosphere, international food
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Generally safe, slightly eclectic. Best to keep valuables secure in the densely crowded market area.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 511 Bathurst streetcar south to BMO — about 20 min
neighborhoods.description: The most culturally vibrant neighbourhood in the city. Vintage shops, cheap food from everywhere, and a genuinely welcoming World Cup atmosphere.

hotels.name: Fairmont Royal York
hotels.distance: 10 min by streetcar to BMO Field
hotels.best_for: Classic luxury, Union Station access, points redemptions

hotels.name: The Anndore House
hotels.distance: 20 min by transit to BMO Field
hotels.best_for: Mid-range budget, boutique feel, subway access

hotels.name: Soho Metropolitan Hotel
hotels.best_for: Nightlife access, boutique luxury, entertainment district

booking_links.label: Browse all Toronto hotels on Booking.com →

bars.name: Real Sports Bar & Grill
bars.notes: Canada's largest sports bar — massive screens, incredible capacity. Expect long lines for major matches. Worth the wait.

bars.name: The Brazen Head
bars.notes: Toronto's oldest Irish pub. Great soccer atmosphere with a neighbourhood crowd.

bars.name: Scallywags Sports Bar
bars.notes: Local favourite with a mixed international crowd. Very welcoming for all nationalities.

bars.name: Soho House Toronto
bars.notes: Members-only rooftop — if you have access, the match-day experience here is exceptional.

bars.name: The Dog's Bollocks
bars.notes: Beloved British pub in the Annex. Packed for every England match, but great for all games.

bars.name: Amsterdam BrewHouse
bars.notes: Lakeside brewery with outdoor patio. Great pre-match and post-match location near BMO Field.

transport.summary: Toronto's TTC streetcar and subway network is practical and reliable for World Cup visitors. Union Station is the central hub connecting GO Train, UP Express from Pearson, and TTC streetcar to BMO Field.
tips: Load a PRESTO card at Pearson or Union for seamless TTC and GO Transit travel
509 or 511 streetcars from Union Station to Exhibition Place — 15 minutes, most direct route
Bike Share Toronto docks are near BMO Field and along the waterfront trail
GO Train extended service from suburbs on major match days — check Metrolinx schedule
The PATH underground walkway connects Downtown hotels — useful in rain between streetcar stops

fan_zones.name: Nathan Phillips Square Fan Festival
fan_zones.location: 100 Queen St W, Toronto City Hall
fan_zones.description: Toronto's most iconic civic square, expected to host a major tournament fan hub with giant screens, live performances, and food representing the nations of the world.

fan_zones.name: Harbourfront Fan Zone
fan_zones.description: Waterfront gathering area with outdoor screens and lake views. A 10-minute walk from BMO Field.

soccer_culture.community_notes: Toronto has arguably the deepest soccer culture in Canada. Toronto FC fills BMO Field, the city has massive supporter groups, and the Italian, Portuguese, Caribbean, and Latin American communities all bring deep football passion to the streets during the World Cup.

tourist_hits.name: CN Tower
tourist_hits.notes: Iconic observation deck with glass floor and EdgeWalk. Book tickets in advance.

tourist_hits.name: Royal Ontario Museum
tourist_hits.notes: World-class natural history and culture collection. Great for a non-match day.

tourist_hits.name: Kensington Market
tourist_hits.notes: Toronto's most eclectic neighbourhood — global street food, vintage shops, open-air market.

tourist_hits.name: Distillery Historic District
tourist_hits.notes: Victorian industrial architecture turned gallery and restaurant district. Beautiful at night.

tourist_hits.name: St. Lawrence Market
tourist_hits.notes: Legendary food market open Tuesday–Sunday. The peameal bacon sandwich is mandatory.

local_favorites.name: Chinatown / Spadina Ave
local_favorites.notes: Authentic Chinese, Vietnamese, and Korean food on one of the most affordable restaurant strips in the city.

local_favorites.name: Little Italy on College St
local_favorites.notes: Great outdoor patios and soccer bar culture. College St fills up on match nights.

local_favorites.name: Toronto Islands
local_favorites.notes: Take the ferry for a 20-minute escape. Beaches, bike paths, and a quiet contrast to the city.

local_favorites.name: Evergreen Brick Works
local_favorites.notes: Former brick factory turned farmers' market and community space. Saturday market is excellent.

areas: King West / Entertainment District — highest density of bars and restaurants
Kensington Market — cheap, global, and authentic
Ossington Ave — craft cocktails and hip restaurants
Little Portugal on Dundas West — expect enormous Portugal fan gatherings
Little Italy on College — great patios, soccer culture

recommendations.name: Pai Northern Thai Kitchen
recommendations.notes: One of Toronto's most beloved restaurants. Book ahead.

recommendations.name: Bar Isabel
recommendations.notes: Spanish tapas and cocktails on Dundas West. Excellent for groups.

recommendations.name: The Black Hoof
recommendations.notes: Charcuterie and cocktails on Dundas West — a local institution.

local_resources.emergency_info: Emergency: 911. Non-emergency Toronto Police: (416) 808-2222. Hospital: Toronto General, 200 Elizabeth St.

walk_bike.walkability_summary: Toronto's Downtown Core, King West, and the waterfront are highly walkable. The stretch from Union Station to BMO Field along the waterfront is a pleasant 25-minute walk.
walk_bike.bikeability_summary: The Martin Goodman Trail along the waterfront is excellent. Bike Share Toronto has docks throughout the city.
walk_bike.bike_share_notes: Bike Share Toronto docks are near Union Station, Exhibition Place, and throughout Downtown. Single rides or day passes available via the Bike Share Toronto app.

pickup_soccer.name: Dufferin Grove Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Informal pickup games most evenings and weekend afternoons. Mixed skill and international crowd.

pickup_soccer.name: Christie Pits Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Multiple fields with active pickup culture. Historic site — passionate local soccer crowd.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Niagara Falls
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Classic day trip. Go train or bus from Union Station. See both Horseshoe Falls and the Canadian side for the best views.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Toronto Islands
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Car-free islands with beaches, bike paths, and a quiet escape from city noise. Ferry tickets are inexpensive — book online.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Muskoka Lakes
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Classic Ontario cottage experience. Rental cottages available for multi-night stays between matches.

safety_tips: Toronto is one of the safest large cities in North America — general tourist areas are low-risk
Downtown and the Entertainment District get crowded on match nights — keep a hand on your belongings
Rideshare is safe and reliable for late-night travel
Be aware of weather changes — Toronto summer storms can arrive with little warning
Carry your hotel address written down in case your phone dies in unfamiliar areas
